script.title: Why Neobanks Like Fi Money Lose Crores #shorts

segments.text: Indian neobanks like Fi Money don't actually hold a banking license.
segments.broll: young person using smartphone app street

segments.text: Under RBI rules, they must partner with traditional banks to hold your deposits.
So when you park paisa, the partner bank keeps the interest margin, not the app.
They mostly earn small commissions on debit card spends and mutual fund sales.
broll_alt: tap to pay mobile phone retail

segments.text: Even after cutting losses by 25%, Fi Money lost ₹153.3 crore as revenue fell.
Without their own lending license, making big money remains a tough climb.
segments.broll: person walking up steep hill outdoors
broll_alt: business executive looking out window night

segments.text: That is why Indian neobanks can't actually accept your money directly.
